headline: Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant begins power generation testing at Unit 1
summary: Unit 1 of Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant has commenced electricity generation testing, a crucial step towards supplying power to the national grid. The process began after receiving regulatory approval for stage C operations.
details: Unit 1 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant began the process of generating electricity at 12:03pm today, a day after receiving regulatory approval to enter stage C. Officials stated that the process began with an increase in pressure and temperature inside the reactor, marking the start of a series of operational tests.

The systematic testing program covers the operation and coordination of the reactor, primary and secondary systems, turbine-generator, electrical systems, instrumentation and control, and protection and safety systems. As reactor power is progressively increased, the performance of major plant systems is monitored and verified under operating conditions.

During the C stage, reactor power will be gradually increased to produce steam, drive the turbine, and generate electricity. The plant's generation capacity will be raised incrementally, with the turbine's functions closely monitored throughout the process.

The start of the power generation process does not mean electricity is being supplied to the national grid yet. The unit must first complete a series of tests under the C stage before grid supply can begin, which officials hope will be possible by the end of this year.

The Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority granted approval yesterday for Unit-1 to enter the C stage and begin the power generation process. Built on the banks of the Padma River in Ishwardi upazila of Pabna, the plant was constructed at a cost of $12.65 billion with Russian financial and technical support.
The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has two VVER-1200 reactors. Once both units are fully operational, the plant is designed to supply 2,400 megawatts of electricity to the national grid.

headline: 22,721 passengers affected as 159 Dhaka-Riyadh flights cancelled
summary: Massive flight cancellations between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia leave thousands of travelers stranded.
details: A total of 159 flights between Dhaka and Riyadh have been cancelled, causing significant disruption to travel plans.
The cancellations have affected 22,721 passengers, many of whom may be traveling for work or religious purposes.
The scale of the disruption is one of the most significant flight cancellations on a single route between Bangladesh and the two cities.
